title: How long until your money doubles?
hook: Money grows 9% a year. Can you work out its doubling time in your head?

doesNotKnow: a mental shortcut for doubling time
how accurate that shortcut is at different rates

misconception: At 9% it takes 100 / 9 = 11 years to double.
objective: The learner can estimate doubling time as 72 divided by the yearly rate, knows it is close (best around 6–10%), and knows 100 ÷ rate is the no-compounding answer.

claims.text: With yearly compounding at rate r, the exact doubling time is ln 2 / ln(1 + r).
claims.source: Solve (1 + r)^t = 2: t = ln 2 / ln(1 + r).

claims.text: At 9% the exact doubling time is about 8.04 years; 72 ÷ 9 = 8.
100 ÷ 9 ≈ 11 years is the doubling time without compounding (9% of the original each year).
The rule of 72 is closest around 6% to 10%: at 3% it gives 24 years (exact 23.4); at 20% it gives 3.6 years (exact 3.8).
The rule of 72 is an approximation for steady yearly compounding, not a forecast of any return.
claims.source: Rule of 72 as an approximation of ln 2 / ln(1 + r); e.g. Brealey, Myers & Allen, Principles of Corporate Finance (future values), or any finance text.

claims.text: 72 suits mental arithmetic because it divides evenly by many common rates (2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12).
